DeepSeek mainnet: fully eager audit role, seam binds all 40 layers, result walker skips modules (#154)

* Run the audit role with nightly prefill CUDA graphs off as well

Nightly SGLang captures prefill graphs under cuda_graph_backend_prefill,
which disable_cuda_graph leaves on. The DeepSeek-V4.1 arena config sets
cuda_graph_backend_prefill=breakable with cuda_graph_max_bs_prefill=16384,
so the "eager" audit role captured 74 prefill shapes and graded each shape's
two dummy warmup passes (every token writes one cache page; stock against
stock p90 0.15-0.65), and never saw a prefill the graph replayed (B300,
2026-10-15, stock-only diagnostic d4 on GPUs 4-7).

_eager_audit_engine() turns both off for the engine worker's audit role
and miner_check's audit phase; a config without the prefill key is left as
it was.

Consumer: engine_worker.isolated_engine_session (audit role) and
miner_check._engine (audit phase). Casualty: the two inline
disable_cuda_graph assignments it replaces.
Docs: validator-guide/fidelity.md.
Net lines: production +13/-3, docs +1/-1, loc baseline +3/-2 (cacheon
ceiling +12, scripts +1 for the note). No deletion was available here.

* Bind every node a slot address names when the model reaches it by several paths

The DeepSeek-V4.1 fork pinned for the arena (nightly 684fea8a, from upstream
`self._next_layer = next_layer`, which registers the next layer as a child
module. With Engram layers 1 and 14 the chains run 1->...->13 and 14->...->39,
and the deduplicating `named_modules()` yields layers 2-13 and 15-39 first as
`model.layers.1._next_layer...` and `model.layers.14._next_layer...`. bind()
matched `model.layers.*.<x>` against that listing, so every per-layer bundle on
the fork images ran and was audited on layers 0, 1 and 14 only (rig bundle arm
claude-g-d1b01-cand: completed calls 4,716 = 3 x 1,572 per slot per rank).

bind() now matches slot addresses against every path
(`named_modules(remove_duplicate=False)`), binds each module once per slot under
its first matching path (a module every layer shares, such as a cached rotary
embedding, still binds once as before), and treats one module that two slots
reach through different paths as the existing overlap error instead of wrapping
it twice. SGLang's loader already walks this graph without a memo
(`model.eval()` after post_load_weights), so the listing terminates; on
DeepSeek-V4.1 it holds about 443 layer subtrees instead of 40.

Consumer: sglang_nodes.install -> ModelRunner.load_model -> bind() in every
served engine. Casualty: supersedes the unmerged dsv4flash commits 5803438f and
288b6635 (PR 146, closed); nothing in the tree.

CPU proof (real bind() and dispatcher on a 40-layer toy wired like the fork's
bind_next; scratch only, no test added): model.layers.*.self_attn and .mlp bind
40 of 40 (were 3), 40 completed calls per slot per forward (were 3), 40 audited
units per slot with 0 violations; `model`, the overlap refusal and a shared
module bind as before; a GLM-shaped model binds identical names before and after.

Docs: the slot contract's node-address definition says a dotted path by which
the served model reaches a module, and that such a module binds once.

Net lines: production +10/-7, docs +3/-3, loc baseline +3/-2 (cacheon ceiling
+3, scripts +1 for the note). No deletion was available: the change supersedes
no path in the tree.

* Skip modules when walking a node's result for graded tensors

With every layer bound, the V4.1 fork's MoE returns a MoEOutput record on
decode calls of 37 of its 40 layers, and that record carries the experts
module. The result walker followed the module's attributes until Python's
recursion limit: every such stock reference failed, the audit refused the
call, and those MLP calls went ungraded while each wrote a ~1,000-frame
traceback (15,412 calls, 2.2 GB of log in one stock-identity check on B300,
2026-10-15). A module holds weights, not an answer; the record's per-call
tensors (the routed rows or their deferred-finalize pieces, and the shared
expert output) are graded as before.

* Run the pristine reference without V4.1 decoder SWA bounded replay

The reference role scores every response position's logprob. With the arena's
enable_decoder_swa_bounded_replay, the V4.1 model runs its late layers over only
a prefill's last window and refuses prompt logprobs, so the reference crashed
and held 2118ab5b after its speed and audit runs (B300, 2026-10-15). Speed and
audit sessions keep the flag. The arena README names fork 4f335dad.

* Fail any audited call under its bar

Owner ruling 2026-10-15: 2118ab5b passed at worst_frac 0.7368 against the
0.75 node bar by pruning routed experts, inside the 2026-09-18 near-miss
allowance (one compared call per 100 within 0.03 of its bar). A compared
call under its bar now fails. Gross calls keep their recorded detail, so
retained audit witnesses regrade unchanged on reopen.

Docs: validator fidelity audit outcomes and the miner failure guide.
Lines: cacheon +7/-10 (ceiling locked at 91885), tests +5/-5, docs +10/-10.

* Treat speed policy 18 as statistical in reward comparisons

Version 18 (portable paired windows) seals min_margin 0 like version 17,
but _reward_min_margin only recognized 17 as statistical and read 18's
sealed 0 as a historical margin. Once a second DeepSeek PASS beat the
first on one baseline, reward_comparisons raised "reward comparison
margin is invalid": the weight offer push failed and the dashboard API
returned 500 from 2026-10-15 23:45Z. Version 18 now uses the ruled 1.5%
statistical margin.

cacheon +3/-2, tests +3/-2 (the statistical test runs for 17 and 18 and
reproduced the live error before the fix), docs +3/-3, loc baseline +4/-3.

* Continue the reward record across declared recommissions

A validator-side recommission changes the arena and incumbent stack digests
even when the stock engine, model and workload stay the same, so the reward
comparison started a fresh record: the e4aced40 audit-gate recommission made
37a3330a (1.0496) a "first PASS" below 97f82e0f (1.0616) and paid it.

The intake metadata key reward_group_continuations maps a later
arena:stack pair to the earlier pair it continues. Reward comparison,
duplicate detection and the stall clock treat the later commission as the
earlier one; chains resolve to their first pair and a cycle is refused.
Non-empty continuations enter the projection's source identity.

* Fail routed-expert pruning beyond stock's prune as its own audit reason

Owner ruling 2026-10-17: the DeepSeek-V4.1 fork's stock E5 prune (budget 0.4,
max count 1) is the reference, and a bundle that prunes more fails even when
its rows stay inside the audit bar. 2118ab5b passed at budget 0.9 and had to
be failed by hand.

The eager audit role now records pruning findings in the slot receipt:

- While the fork's prune module is loaded, every audited call compares its
  settings in the engine with the literal values in its installed source. A
  bundle that raises them makes stock's own reference prune as much as it does.
- A node holding exactly one MoE block that stock prunes (model.layers.*.mlp)
  answers each audited decode or verify call once more with stock pruned one
  step heavier, alternating budget + 0.1 and max count + 1. On rows where that
  reference sits more than twice the row tolerance from stock, a candidate
  nearer the reference than stock dropped what stock keeps; a row inside the
  tolerance never can be. A pooled window of at least 64 such rows that is
  mostly nearer the reference is a finding.

The receipt carries the count as an optional pruned fact, absent at zero, so
honest receipts, retained witnesses and their digests keep their bytes. The
gate fails any finding before every other fault, and the witness names the
reason routed_expert_pruning; the runner, the continuation stage exit and the
stage-exit check all take the reason from the witness, which replaces the
duplicated audit reason table. The whole model node is not graded against a
heavier reference: downstream routing flips leave a pruned and an honest stack
about equally far from both references. Whole-model pruning in a bundle's own
kernels remains for the row bar and owner disposition under the same reason.

The loc baseline also restores the branch raises that merge 26b7cbb5 dropped.

* Hold the first claim for the operator's pruning review

Owner ruling 2026-10-17: routed-expert pruning beyond the fork's stock prune
fails. The audit-time check cannot see a whole-model bundle that prunes inside
its own kernels: on the exact worker image 7bd15e45 (0.7 / 3) and 73263b71
(0.65 / 2) passed their audits at worst_frac 0.914 with no row flagged.

Before a bundle's first claim, admission now reads the verdict the operator's
review wrote for it under the standing supervisor's pruning_review_root: pass
admits it, fail fails it as routed_expert_pruning before any GPU time, and a
missing verdict holds the claim. A verdict binds its reservation ID and content
hash; anything else stops the stage. The review (Claude Opus 5.5 reading the
bundle's source) runs outside this repository and its prompt is not published.
An empty pruning_review_root claims bundles unreviewed, as before.

* Boot each engine on its sealed schedulers' NUMA node

SGLang ranks first-touch their host-resident tables inside sgl.Engine()
(DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram: ~200 GB of huge pages per TP2 lane). SGLang's own
NUMA bind needs memory-policy permission the OCI runtime does not grant,
and the sealed cpu_pins apply only after the engine returns, so the tables
landed on whichever socket each rank happened to run. On the Lium 4x B300
pair (lanes on different sockets) one boot put both lanes' tables on the
remote socket (cgroup memory.numa_stat, 2026-10-17).

The engine worker now sets its affinity to the NUMA node(s) of the lane's
sealed scheduler vCPUs before building the engine; spawned ranks inherit
it, and the existing post-boot pins narrow it as before. No plan, no change.

Consumer: isolated_engine_session, every lane launch with sealed cpu_pins.
Supersedes nothing. Lines: +21 runtime, +20 tests, +4/-1 docs,
+6/-4 scripts (LOC note and ceilings).

* Run the pruning review after the queue binds to its commission

The first claim after a recommission found every queued row bound to the
previous commission's baseline segment. The claim preview selects only rows
bound to the current one, so admission saw an empty preview and passed
without reading a verdict; the commissioned-incumbent binding then ran and
the claim took the queue head. On the Lium recommission (2026-10-17) this
claimed 747f8d71, whose review verdict was fail; the run was cancelled
before any window.

Admission now runs after the binding, as the claim does. The binding is
idempotent and already ran before every claim.

Consumer: RecoverableQualificationDispatcher._claim_or_reopen. Supersedes
nothing. Lines: +4/-4 runtime, +31 tests, +4/-2 scripts (LOC note and
ceilings).

* Preview admission as the claimer under the arena's capacity

The pruning-review admission previewed the next claim with the selector's
defaults: no owner and a capacity of one active lease. On a node running two
pairs, the other pair's active lease emptied that preview, the review loop
admitted on nothing, and the claim bound the unreviewed head: reviewed
pruner 73263b71 reached the GPUs on the Verda node (2026-10-18). The preview
now takes the claimer's owner and the arena's max_active_qualifications,
exactly as the claim selects; the operator CLI preview keeps its defaults.

Consumer: recoverable_qualification_dispatcher -> pruning_review.admit.
Supersedes nothing. Lines +57 / -13 (runtime +8, tests +36, notes +2); the
shared review-file helper replaces the per-test copy. No docs change: the
gate now behaves as chain-loop.md and pipeline.md already describe it.
